title: GradNexa User Guide
tagline: From Engineering Graduate to Industry-Ready Professional.
principles: Scores come from fixed rules, never from an AI model. Each score shows its rule version and the evidence behind it.
Readiness (how prepared you are) and eligibility (whether you meet a company's rules) are never merged into one number.
There are no placement predictions: you see levels and plain statements only.
Nothing is hard-coded: departments, skills, roles, weights and eligibility rules are all set up by your college.

roles.does: Builds a profile, takes assessments, sees readiness and skill gaps, follows a 30-day plan, practises interviews, analyses a resume, checks jobs.
Sees assigned students; writes assessments, questions, resources, interview questions; manages knowledge documents.
Placement dashboard; manages companies and jobs.
Aggregate view of the departments assigned to them (no individual student records).
Configures everything for the college and can use all staff tools.

overview.title: Student builds evidence
overview.summary: Registers, completes the profile, takes assessments.

procedures.title: Register a new account
procedures.summary: Create your student account with your college code.
before: Your college's code (ask your college if you do not have it).

steps.do: Open the application and go to **Register** (a link on the login page).
Fill in **Full name**, **Email** and **Password** (at least 8 characters).
steps.detail: Use an email address you can open: it is used to reset your password.

steps.do: Type your **College code**.
Click **Create account**.
steps.expect: You are taken to the login page with a note that your account was created.

result: A Student account in your college.

problems.fix: All four fields must be filled in.

problems.problem: An error about the college code.
problems.fix: Check the code with your college; codes are not case-guessable.

procedures.title: Log in
procedures.summary: Sign in and land on your role's home page.
before: An account (see Register; staff accounts are created by an admin changing a registered user's role).

steps.do: Go to the **Log in** page and enter your **Email** and **Password**.
Click **Sign in**.
steps.expect: You land on your home page: Student - Dashboard; Faculty - Faculty dashboard; TPO - Placement dashboard; HOD - HOD dashboard; Admin - Profile.

steps.do: A student who has not finished their profile is sent to onboarding automatically.

result: A signed-in session. It refreshes itself; after 7 days you must sign in again.

problems.fix: Repeated failed sign-ins are rate-limited. Wait a minute and try again.
Use **Forgot password?** (next procedure).

procedures.title: Reset a forgotten password
procedures.summary: Get a reset link by email.
before: Email sending must be configured by your operator.

steps.do: On the login page click **Forgot password?**.
Enter your **Email** and click **Send reset link**.
steps.expect: A message says a link has been sent if an account exists (it never reveals whether the email is registered).

steps.do: Open the email and click the link.
Enter **New password** and **Confirm password**, then click **Reset password**.
Log in with the new password.

result: Access restored.

problems.fix: Check spam; ask your operator whether email (SMTP) is configured. The link expires after 30 minutes.

procedures.title: Edit your name and log out
procedures.summary: Your profile page and signing out.

steps.do: Open **Profile** (admins, TPOs, HODs and students all have it in the menu).
Change **Full name** and click **Save changes**.
steps.detail: Email and role are shown for reference and cannot be changed here.

steps.do: To sign out click **Log out** at the top right.

result: Updated name; session ended on log out.

groups.title: Admin: set up the college
groups.intro: Follow these in order. Each step feeds the next. Students only see useful results after the chain is complete.

procedures.title: 1. Create skill categories and skills
procedures.summary: The shared vocabulary used by assessments, roles, resources, resumes and jobs.
before: Departments exist (created when the college was installed).

steps.do: Click **Skills** in the top menu.
steps.expect: The **Skills** page opens with a Category form and a Skill form.

steps.do: In the category form enter **Category name** (for example Programming).
steps.detail: Choose **Scope**: Common (every department) or Department (then pick the **Department**).

steps.do: Click **Add category**. Repeat for each category.
In the skill form enter **Skill name**, choose its **Category**, optionally add a **Description**, then click **Add skill**. Repeat for each skill.
To change something later, pick it in the list, edit, and click **Save category** or **Save skill** (**Cancel** discards).

result: A skill list that every other module refers to.

problems.problem: 'Select a department for a department-scoped category.'
problems.fix: Either set Scope to Common or choose a Department.

procedures.title: 2. Create career roles and their required skills
procedures.summary: Roles students can aim for, with the level required for each skill.
before: Skills exist (step 1).

steps.do: Click **Career roles** in the top menu, then **New role**.
Enter **Role name**, optionally **Department** and **Description**, keep **Active** ticked, and click **Create role**.
In the skills editor choose a skill under **Add a skill** and click **Add skill**. Repeat for every skill the role needs.
For each skill set **Required level** (0 to 100; new rows start at 60) and **Weight** (greater than 0; starts at 1).
steps.detail: Required level is the target a student's skill score is compared with. Weight says how much that skill matters for this role.

steps.do: Click **Save skills**.

result: The yardstick that skill gaps and role readiness are measured against.

problems.fix: Correct the number; weights must be above 0.

procedures.title: 3. Create and activate the readiness rule
procedures.summary: Category weights, level bands and gap thresholds. There are no defaults.
before: Skill categories (step 1) and roles (step 2).

steps.do: Click **Readiness rules** in the top menu, then **Create new version**.
steps.detail: It is prefilled from the active version if one exists. Rules are immutable: changing scoring always means a new version.

steps.do: Under **Category weights** enter a weight for each skill category you want counted. Leave one blank to exclude it.
steps.detail: Weights are relative to each other, not percentages.

steps.do: Under **Level thresholds** give each level a name and **Minimum score** (for example Needs improvement 0, Developing 50, Strong 75). Use **Add level** for more.
Under **Gap thresholds** set **High priority at gap of at least** and **Medium priority at gap of at least**.
Click **Create version**.
steps.expect: 'Version N created. It is inactive until you activate it.'

steps.do: Click **Activate** on that version and confirm **Activate this rule version?**.
steps.expect: It becomes the active rule; older results keep the version they used.

result: Readiness can now be computed, and every result is explainable by rule version.

problems.problem: Students see 'Not enough evidence yet' for everyone.
problems.fix: Check a rule is active and that assessments covering the role's skills are published.

procedures.note: These numbers are institutional policy. Agree them with your placement and academic leads before activating.

procedures.title: 4. Create an assessment and add questions
procedures.summary: Tests students take to produce skill scores. Assessments are versioned.
before: Skills exist (step 1).

steps.do: Click **Assessments** in the top menu (**Manage assessments**).
Fill **Title**, **Type**, optionally **Department**, **Time limit (minutes, optional)**, **Max attempts (optional)** and **Negative marking (0 to 1)**.
Click **Create assessment**. It starts as a draft.
Click the assessment's title to open it, then click **Add question**.
Write the **Question**, choose its **Skill**, **Difficulty** and **Marks**, add answer options with **Add option** and tick the correct one(s), then **Add question**. Repeat for every question.
Back on the list, click **Publish** and confirm **Publish assessment?**.
steps.detail: Students can then attempt it, and it can no longer be edited.

result: A published assessment that produces skill scores.

problems.problem: You need to change a published assessment.
problems.fix: Click **New version** to copy it into a new draft; **Archive** retires the old one (students can no longer start it).
Only drafts with no attempts can be deleted.

procedures.title: 5. Browse the question bank
procedures.summary: See all questions across assessments.
before: At least one assessment with questions.

steps.do: Click **Question bank** in the top menu.
Filter by **Skill**, **Difficulty** or **Assessment** to review coverage.
Use it to spot skills or difficulties with too few questions, then add questions inside the relevant assessment (procedure 4).

result: Confidence that every skill has enough questions.

procedures.title: 6. Add and approve learning resources
procedures.summary: Courses and links the 30-day plan is built from.
before: Skills exist (step 1).

steps.do: Click **Learning resources** in the top menu.
Choose the **Skill**, enter **Title** and **URL** (starts with https://), optionally a **Description**, then click **Add resource**.
In the list click **Approve** on a resource and confirm **Approve this resource?**.
steps.detail: Only approved resources are shown to students and used in plans. **Unapprove** withdraws one.

steps.do: Use **Filter by skill** and **Approval** to find resources still waiting.

result: Approved material the plan generator can use.

problems.problem: A student's plan has no resource for a skill.
problems.fix: Add and approve a resource for that skill.

procedures.title: 7. Add interview questions with a rubric
procedures.summary: Questions used in mock interviews, scored against a rubric.
before: Career roles exist (step 2) if you want role-specific questions.

steps.do: Click **Interview questions** in the top menu.
Enter the **Prompt**, **Competency** and **Minimum words**; optionally choose **Role** and **Skill**.
Fill the rubric: the points a good answer should cover (the keywords or criteria used to score it).
Click **Create question**.
Use **Filter by role** and **Status** to review the list.

result: Mock interviews can be scored.

problems.fix: Add active questions for that role or generic ones (no role).

procedures.title: 8. Add companies
procedures.summary: The recruiting companies jobs belong to.

steps.do: Click **Companies** in the top menu.
Enter **Company name**, optionally **Description** and **Website**, and click **Create company**.
Use **Deactivate** or **Reactivate** to hide a company without deleting it; **Delete** removes it permanently.

result: Companies to attach jobs to.

procedures.title: 9. Create a job with skills and eligibility, then publish
procedures.summary: Postings students see, with eligibility checked separately from readiness.
before: A company (step 8) and, ideally, a career role (step 2).

steps.do: Click **Jobs** in the top menu, then **New job**.
Choose the **Company**, enter **Job title** and **Job description**, optionally a **Career role** and an **Application deadline** (a date), then click **Create job**.
steps.expect: 'Job created as a draft.' Students cannot see it yet.

steps.do: Open the job (click **Manage job ...**).
Set the required skills: **Add a skill**, **Required level**, **Weight**, then **Save skills**.

Set the eligibility rule: **Departments**, **Minimum CGPA** (0-10) with its **CGPA basis** (for example Latest semester or Average of all semesters), **Maximum arrears**, **Minimum attendance %** (0-100) and **Graduation years** (comma-separated, for example 2026, 2027). Click **Save eligibility rule**.
steps.detail: Leave a field empty to apply no rule for it. **Remove rule** deletes the whole rule.

steps.do: Click **Publish** and confirm.
steps.expect: The job is visible to students, with Met / Not met / Unknown per criterion.

result: A live job posting with its eligibility rule.

problems.problem: You closed a job by mistake.
problems.fix: Closing is permanent: a closed job cannot be edited or reopened. Create a new job instead.
Only draft jobs can be deleted.

procedures.title: 10. Upload and approve knowledge documents
procedures.summary: Guides and policies that Knowledge search and the Assistant can cite.

steps.do: Click **Knowledge base** in the top menu.
Enter **Title**, choose **Source type**, optionally a **Department**, choose the **Document file** (PDF, DOCX, TXT or MD) and click **Upload document**.
Click the document to check its **Chunks** (the passages it was split into), then **Close details**.
Click **Approve** and confirm **Approve this document?**.
steps.detail: Only approved documents are searchable or citable. **Archive** removes it from search; **Delete** removes it and its chunks.

result: Cited answers in Knowledge search and the Assistant.

problems.fix: Only PDF, DOCX, TXT and MD under 10 MB are accepted; scanned images need selectable text (no OCR).

procedures.title: 11. Assign a HOD to departments
procedures.summary: Which departments each HOD sees on their dashboard.
before: A user whose role is HOD (set it first on the Users and students page).

steps.do: Click **HOD assignments** in the left menu.
Choose the **HOD** from the list (it shows only users whose role is HOD) and the **Department**, then click **Add assignment**.
To undo, click **Remove** on the row and **Confirm remove**.

result: The HOD dashboard shows aggregates for those departments.

problems.problem: The HOD list is empty ('No HOD users yet').
problems.fix: Nobody has the HOD role yet. Open **Users and students**, click **Change role** on the person and choose HOD.

procedures.title: 12. Choose which data tools the Assistant may use
procedures.summary: Switch the Assistant's read-only data tools on or off for your college.

steps.do: Click **MCP tools** in the top menu.
Use the switch next to a tool (**Enable ...**) to turn it on or off. Each tool is limited to the roles shown.

result: Control over what the Assistant may read. Turning a tool off stops the Assistant using it.

procedures.title: 13. Test the student journey before announcing
procedures.summary: Walk the whole path once as a student.
before: Steps 1 to 12 done.

steps.do: Register a test student (Register a new account) and log in in a private window.
Complete onboarding, then take a published assessment.
Open **Readiness**, choose a role, click **Compute / refresh**; then open **Skill gaps**.
Generate a 30-day plan; open **Jobs** and check eligibility.
Fix whatever is missing upstream and repeat.

result: Confidence that the numbers look sensible.

problems.fix: The role's skills are not covered by a published assessment the student attempted.

procedures.title: Users and students: see who registered and set roles
procedures.summary: See everyone in your college, create Faculty, TPO, HOD and Admin accounts by changing a role, and assign students to faculty.
before: People have registered normally (everyone starts as a Student).

steps.do: Click **Users and students** in the left menu.
steps.expect: A table of everyone in your college: name, email, role, department, roll number, graduation year, whether the student's profile is complete, and the join date.

steps.do: Find people with **Search name, email or roll number**, the **Role** filter and the **Student department** filter, then click **Search**.
steps.detail: Results are paged (25 per page) with **Previous** and **Next**.

steps.do: To make someone Faculty, TPO, HOD or Admin, click **Change role** on their row, choose the **New role**, and click **Apply**.
Read the confirmation and click **Change role**.
steps.expect: '<Name> is now <Role>.' The change applies immediately, even to someone already signed in.
steps.detail: Leaving Faculty removes that person's faculty-to-student assignments; leaving HOD removes their department assignments. The screen tells you how many were removed.

steps.do: Open the **Faculty assignments** tab to give a faculty member their students: choose the **Faculty member**, type a name, email or roll number in **Find a student**, click **Find student**, pick the **Student**, then click **Add assignment**.
To undo an assignment click **Remove** on its row and **Confirm remove**.

result: Staff users who can use the staff pages, and faculty who see their assigned students.

problems.problem: There is no Change role button on a row.
problems.fix: You cannot change your own role, and a super-admin account cannot be changed from here.
Ask another admin to change it; this prevents locking yourself out.

problems.problem: A faculty member's dashboard is empty.
problems.fix: They have no students assigned yet: use the Faculty assignments tab.

procedures.note: Every role change is written to the audit log. Student names and emails are personal data: only promote people you trust to Admin.

groups.title: College configuration (with samples)
groups.intro: Everything the college decides before students see useful results. All values in the sample tables are examples to show the format, not recommendations: your college chooses its own.

procedures.title: What the college configures: the checklist
procedures.summary: Every configurable item, where it lives, what it depends on and what it changes for students.

tables.title: Configuration checklist (in dependency order)
columns: What students see once it is done
rows: Set at install (API for later additions)
A department list to choose from in onboarding
Skill names on scores, gaps and plans
A list of roles to explore, and the target for gaps
Job list with Met / Not met / Unknown
Cited answers in Assistant and Knowledge search
A user with the HOD role (set on Users and students)
Users and students, Faculty assignments tab
A user with the Faculty role (set on Users and students)
What the Assistant is allowed to read
Limits such as upload size and sign-in rate limits
tables.caption: Work top to bottom: later rows depend on earlier ones.

result: A complete picture of what must be configured, who does it and in what order.

procedures.title: Departments
procedures.summary: The departments in your college. Nothing is hard-coded: the app has no built-in department list.

steps.do: The operator creates departments when installing (the **--departments** option of the seed command, written as Name:CODE pairs separated by commas).
Departments added later are created through the API (**POST /api/v1/admin/departments**); there is no screen yet.

tables.title: Sample departments
tables.caption: Example only. Use your own departments and codes.

result: Students pick their department in onboarding; skill categories, assessments and job eligibility can be limited to departments.

problems.problem: A student cannot find their department.
problems.fix: It has not been created yet; ask the operator.

procedures.title: Skill categories and skills
procedures.summary: The shared vocabulary for assessments, roles, resources, resumes and jobs.

steps.do: On **Skills**, add each category with **Category name** and **Scope** (Common, or Department plus the **Department**), then **Add category**.
Add each skill with **Skill name**, its **Category** and an optional **Description**, then **Add skill**.

tables.title: Sample skill setup
tables.caption: Example only. Category weights in the readiness rule apply per category, so group skills the way you want them weighted.

result: A skill list that every other item refers to.

problems.problem: Two skills with almost the same name.
problems.fix: Keep one name per skill; scores, gaps, resumes and jobs all match by skill.

procedures.title: Career roles and required skills
procedures.summary: What each role needs. This is the yardstick for role readiness and skill gaps.

steps.do: On **Career roles** click **New role**; enter **Role name**, optional **Department** and **Description**, keep **Active** ticked; **Create role**.
Add skills with **Add a skill**; set **Required level** (0 to 100) and **Weight** (above 0) for each; **Save skills**.

tables.title: Sample role: Backend Developer
tables.caption: Required level is the target (0 to 100). Weight is how much the skill counts toward this role's score. New rows start at level 60, weight 1.

result: Students can explore the role, and readiness and gaps are measured against these levels.

problems.fix: It has no required skills yet.

procedures.title: Readiness rule: weights, levels and gap thresholds
procedures.summary: There are no default numbers. The college defines them, and every change creates a new version.
before: Skill categories and career roles exist.

steps.do: On **Readiness rules** click **Create new version**.
Enter a weight per skill category, the level names with their **Minimum score**, and the two gap thresholds; **Create version**; then **Activate** it.

tables.title: Sample rule: category weights (general readiness)
tables.caption: Weights are relative to each other; a blank category is left out.

tables.title: Sample rule: level thresholds
tables.caption: A student's level is the one with the highest minimum score that their overall score reaches. One level must start at 0.

tables.title: Sample rule: gap thresholds
rows: High priority at gap of at least
Medium priority at gap of at least
tables.caption: Any gap above 0 but below the Medium value is Low priority.

tables.title: Worked example: role readiness for Backend Developer
tables.caption: Role score = weighted mean over skills with evidence = (80x2 + 50x2) / 4 = 65.00, which is Developing in the sample levels. Coverage = weight with evidence / total weight = 4 / 6 = 66.67%, shown next to the score so a thin result is visible. Skills with no evidence are left out, never counted as 0.

result: Readiness levels and gap priorities can now be computed; each result is stamped with the rule version.

problems.problem: You want different weights next term.
problems.fix: Create a new version and activate it. Old results keep the version they used.
No rule is active, or students have no assessment results for the skills.

procedures.note: Weights and thresholds are institutional policy. Agree them with your placement and academic leads before activating.

procedures.title: Assessments and questions
procedures.summary: Tests that produce skill scores. Scoring is fixed by rules; negative marking is configurable.
before: Skills exist.

steps.do: On **Assessments** fill **Title**, **Type**, optional **Department**, **Time limit (minutes, optional)**, **Max attempts (optional)** and **Negative marking (0 to 1)**; **Create assessment**.
Open it, **Add question** for each question, then **Publish**.

tables.title: Sample assessment settings
rows: One of APTITUDE, TECHNICAL, COMMUNICATION, ROLE_SPECIFIC, DEPARTMENT_SPECIFIC, CUSTOM
A wrong answer loses 0.25 x the question's marks; 0 means none

tables.title: Sample question
rows: Which keyword defines a function in Python?
A: func   B: def (correct)   C: function   D: lambda only
tables.caption: Several options can be marked correct; the student must choose exactly the correct set (no partial credit).

tables.title: Worked example: scoring one attempt (10 questions, 1 mark each, negative marking 0.25)
tables.caption: Scores never go below 0. A skill's stored score is the percentage from the latest attempt that covered it.

result: Published assessments produce the skill scores everything else is built on.

problems.problem: You need to change a published test.
problems.fix: Use New version; Archive the old one.

procedures.title: Learning resources
procedures.summary: The approved material the 30-day plan is built from.
before: Skills exist.

steps.do: On **Learning resources** choose the **Skill**, enter **Title** and **URL**, optional **Description**; **Add resource**.
Click **Approve** on each resource you trust. Unapproved ones are never shown to students.

tables.title: Sample resources
tables.caption: Example links only; use your own vetted resources.

result: Students get plan items only from approved resources; a skill with none gets no item.

procedures.title: Interview questions and rubrics
procedures.summary: Mock-interview questions scored by a keyword rubric (not by an AI).

steps.do: On **Interview questions** enter **Prompt**, **Competency**, **Minimum words** and optionally **Role** and **Skill**.
Add rubric concepts: each has a name, **keywords** and a **weight**. **Create question**.

tables.title: Sample question and rubric
tables.caption: Prompt: 'What is a primary key in a database?'  Competency: Technical.  Minimum words: 20.

tables.title: Worked example: scoring an answer
rows: Primary key definition and no duplicates
tables.caption: Score = weights of covered concepts / total weights x 100. A concept is covered when any of its keywords appears in the answer.

result: Mock interviews return a score per question, plus a disclaimer that it is practice feedback.

procedures.title: Companies, jobs and eligibility rules
procedures.summary: What students see for each posting, and the rules eligibility is checked against.
before: A company exists; ideally a career role.

steps.do: On **Companies** add the company; on **Jobs** click **New job** and fill the details.
Open the job: set required skills and the eligibility rule, then **Publish**.

tables.title: Sample eligibility rule
rows: Other option: Average of all semesters
tables.caption: Leave a field empty to apply no rule for it.

tables.title: What three sample students see
rows: CGPA Met, Arrears Met, Attendance Met
CGPA Met, Arrears Met, Attendance Unknown
tables.caption: Unknown means data is missing, not failure. Eligibility is never part of readiness. A job with no rule shows 'No automatic criteria'.

result: Students see the job with eligibility per rule and a skill-fit view.

problems.problem: A closed job needs to come back.
problems.fix: Closing is permanent. Create a new job.

procedures.title: Knowledge documents
procedures.summary: Documents the Assistant and Knowledge search may cite. Only approved ones are searchable.

steps.do: On **Knowledge base** enter **Title**, choose **Source type**, optional **Department**, pick the **Document file**; **Upload document**.
Check the **Chunks**, then **Approve** it.

tables.title: Source types and samples
tables.caption: Accepted files: PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD up to 10 MB with selectable text.

result: Cited answers; with nothing approved on a topic the Assistant says it does not have enough approved information.

procedures.title: Who sees what: HODs, faculty and Assistant tools
procedures.summary: Assignments and switches that scope what staff and the Assistant can read.
before: Users with the Faculty or HOD role (change roles on Users and students).

steps.do: **HOD assignments:** choose the **HOD** and the **Department**, then **Add assignment**.
**Faculty assignments:** on **Users and students**, open the **Faculty assignments** tab and use **Add assignment**.
**MCP tools:** switch tools on or off for your college.

tables.title: Sample assignments
rows: HOD dashboard shows aggregates for those two departments only
Students 101, 102 and 103 (one assignment per faculty-student pair)
Faculty dashboard lists exactly those three students

tables.title: The Assistant's data tools (all read-only)
rows: Name, department, roll number, graduation year
Plan progress and latest readiness summary
A job's eligibility rule and the student's evaluation
A company and the skills of its open jobs
A job and its required skills
tables.caption: A tool you switch off is no longer used by the Assistant. Students can only ever read their own records.

result: Staff see only what they are assigned; the Assistant reads only what you allow.

problems.problem: A person is missing from the HOD or faculty list.
problems.fix: Their role has not been set yet: use Change role on Users and students.

procedures.title: Technical settings (set by your operator)
procedures.summary: Limits that are not on any screen. They are server settings, and the values below are the defaults.

tables.title: Settings and defaults
rows: How long a sign-in token lasts before it refreshes
How long before a user must sign in again
How long a reset link works
Sign-in and sign-up attempts per IP
How documents are split for search

Email for password reset; empty means no email
Which sites may call the API

procedures.title: Decisions your college must make
procedures.summary: Policy choices the application cannot make for you. Nothing here is pre-set.

rows: Decide how much each skill category counts toward general readiness
Decide what counts as Strong or Needs improvement
Decide when a gap is High or Medium priority

result: A written set of choices to configure, agreed by the college.

procedures.title: 1. Complete onboarding
procedures.summary: A three-step wizard shown on your first login.
before: You registered and logged in.

steps.do: Step 1 of 3, **Personal details**: enter **Roll number**, **Graduation year** and **Phone**, then click **Next**.
Step 2 of 3, **Academics**: add your semester records (see the next procedure for the fields), then **Next**. **Back** returns to the previous step.
Step 3 of 3, **Department**: choose your department and click **Confirm and finish**.
steps.expect: You are taken to your Dashboard.

result: A complete profile. Until it is complete you are sent back here.

problems.fix: Ask your admin to add it.

procedures.title: 2. Keep your academic records accurate
procedures.summary: Semester CGPA, arrears and attendance. Job eligibility is calculated from these.
before: Onboarding done.

steps.do: Click **Academics** in the menu.
Fill **Semester (1-12)**, **CGPA (0-10)**, **Active arrears** and **Attendance % (optional)**, then click **Add record**.
To correct one, choose it, change the values and click **Update record** (**Cancel** discards).

result: Accurate eligibility results.

problems.fix: A value is missing, for example attendance. Add it here; nothing is guessed.

procedures.title: 3. Add projects and certifications
procedures.summary: Your work and certificates.

steps.do: Click **Projects & Certifications** in the menu.
Under **Add project** enter **Title**, optionally **Description** and **URL**, add the **Skills** you used, and click **Add project**.
Under **Add certification** enter **Name**, optionally **Issuer** and **Issued on**, and click **Add certification**.
Use **Delete** to remove an entry.

result: A fuller profile.

procedures.title: 4. Take an assessment
procedures.summary: Tests that produce your skill scores.
before: Your admin has published assessments.

steps.do: Click **Assessments** in the menu.
steps.expect: Published tests are listed with their time limit and attempts.

steps.do: Click **Start** (or **Resume** if you already began one).
Answer the questions. **Question navigator** jumps between them; **Time remaining** and **Answered questions** show progress. Answers save as you go.
Click **Submit** and confirm **Submit your attempt?** with **Confirm submit**.
steps.detail: If time runs out the attempt is submitted for you.

steps.do: Read the result page: your score and the **Skill breakdown**.

result: Skill scores, the evidence everything else is built on.

problems.fix: The maximum attempts are used; ask your faculty or admin.

procedures.title: 5. Review your attempt history
procedures.summary: Every attempt is kept.
before: At least one attempt.

steps.do: Click **History** in the menu.
Click **View result** on any attempt to see its score and skill breakdown.

result: A record of your progress.

procedures.title: 6. Explore careers and set goals
procedures.summary: Find roles and mark the ones you want.
before: Your admin has created career roles.

steps.do: Click **Careers** in the menu (**Career explorer**) and type in **Search roles** (for example Backend).
Open a role to see **Required skills** (with required level and weight) and **My readiness for this role**.
Use **Add ... to my goals** to mark it as a goal. Your goals appear under **My goals** (reorder with the move buttons, then **Save goals**).
Click **View skill gaps** to jump to the gaps for that role.

result: One or more target roles.

procedures.title: 7. See your readiness
procedures.summary: Overall and role-specific readiness, with evidence.
before: Skill scores from at least one assessment, and an active readiness rule.

steps.do: Click **Readiness** in the menu (**Placement readiness**).
Choose a **Career role** and click **Compute / refresh**.
Read the level and score, the category breakdown, the skill scores behind it, and the rule version. **Readiness history** shows earlier results.

result: Your readiness level for that role, fully explained.

problems.fix: Go back to **Assessments** and take ones covering that role's skills, then Compute / refresh again.

procedures.title: 8. Read your skill gaps
procedures.summary: Required level versus your level, ranked.
before: Readiness computed for the role.

steps.do: Click **Skill gaps** in the menu and choose the role.
For each skill read the required level, your current level, the gap and its priority: High, Medium or Low.

result: Know exactly what to improve first.

problems.problem: 'Compute your readiness for this role first'.
problems.fix: Open **Readiness** and click Compute / refresh for that role.

procedures.title: 9. Generate and follow your 30-day plan
procedures.summary: Weekly items built from your gaps and approved learning resources.
before: Readiness computed for a role
Approved learning resources for your gap skills.

steps.do: Click **Plan** in the menu (**30-day plan**).
Choose the **Role** (or **All roles**) and **Skills per week**, then click **Generate 30-day plan**.
Work through each week. On each item set its status to **To do**, **In progress** or **Done**.
After finishing items and new assessments, click **Refresh readiness (reassess)** to compare your new level (**Reassessment comparison**).
To start over click **Generate a new plan** and confirm; earlier plans stay under **Plan history**.

result: A concrete weekly study plan and a measured before/after.

problems.fix: Tell your faculty or admin. Plans never invent resources.

procedures.title: 10. Practise a mock interview
procedures.summary: Rubric-scored practice; it is feedback, not a prediction.
before: Interview questions have been added by your college.

steps.do: Click **Interview** in the menu (**Mock interview**).
Choose a **Role** and **Number of questions (1-10)**, then click **Start**.
Type an answer for each question; **Question navigator** moves between them.
Click **Finish interview** and confirm **Finish this interview?**.
steps.expect: A result page with a score and feedback per question against the rubric.

steps.do: Earlier sessions are listed under **Interview history**.

result: Practice feedback per question.

problems.fix: Your admin must add interview questions for it.

procedures.title: 11. Upload and analyse your resume
procedures.summary: See which of your college's skills your resume shows, linked to the source text.
before: A PDF or DOCX resume of up to 10 MB with selectable text.

steps.do: Click **Resume** in the menu, choose the **Resume file** and click **Upload resume**.
On the uploaded resume click **Analyze**.
Optionally choose a **Target role**, a **Compare with a job posting**, or paste a **Job description**, then click **Run analysis**.

Read the results: **Sections found**, skills **Found in resume** and **Missing from resume**, and (if you compared) the **Job description match**. Click a skill to highlight where it appears in your text.
Use **Delete resume** to remove a resume.

result: Evidence-linked findings; nothing is invented.

problems.fix: Only PDF and DOCX up to 10 MB; scanned images are not read (no OCR).

procedures.title: 12. Check jobs and eligibility
procedures.summary: Open postings, with eligibility shown separately from readiness.
before: Academic records filled in; jobs published by your college.

steps.do: Click **Jobs** in the menu.
Use **Search** (title, company or role) and the **Eligibility** filter.
Read each job's badge: **Meets configured criteria**, **Does not meet configured criteria**, **Some data missing** or **No automatic criteria**.
Open a job to see each rule marked **Met**, **Not met** or **Unknown** with the numbers compared, plus **skill fit** against the job's required skills.

result: Clarity on which jobs you meet the rules for and which skills to add.

problems.fix: That record is missing; complete it under Academics. Unknown is not a failure.

procedures.title: 13. Use your dashboard
procedures.summary: Everything in one place.

steps.do: Click **Dashboard** in the menu.
Read **Role readiness**, **Top skill gaps**, **Career goals** and **Recent assessments**; use **Quick links** to jump to the next action.

result: Your next best step.

problems.problem: A panel says there is not enough evidence.
problems.fix: That is honest, not an error: take assessments for that area.

procedures.title: 14. Ask the Assistant and search knowledge
procedures.summary: Answers from your own results and approved documents, with citations.

steps.do: Click **Assistant** in the menu.
Type **Your question**, optionally choose a **Career role** or **Job**, and click **Ask**. **Example questions** give ideas.
Read the answer: readiness and eligibility appear in separate sections and quoted material has citations.
To read the sources yourself click **Knowledge**, type in **Search** and click **Search**.

result: Cited answers. The Assistant does not use a language model in this version.

problems.problem: 'I don't have enough approved information to answer this confidently.'
problems.fix: No approved document covers it. Ask an admin to upload and approve one.

procedures.title: TPO: use the placement dashboard
procedures.summary: College-wide readiness and placement analytics.
before: Students have profiles and assessment attempts.

steps.do: Click **Placement dashboard** in the menu.
Use the **Department** filter and **Refresh**.
Read the summary (students, profiles complete, with a readiness score, with a submitted assessment) and the analytics: role readiness, company eligibility counts and progress trends.

result: Where to focus preparation. Levels and counts only, never probabilities.

procedures.title: TPO: manage companies and jobs
procedures.summary: Same screens as the Admin placement steps.

steps.do: Follow the Admin procedures **8. Add companies** and **9. Create a job with skills and eligibility, then publish**.

result: Jobs students can see with eligibility.

procedures.title: Faculty: support your assigned students
procedures.summary: Your assigned students only.
before: An admin has assigned students to you.

steps.do: Click **Faculty dashboard** in the menu.
Read the summary: **Assigned students**, **With a readiness score**, **Needing support**.
In the table sort by **Needs support** and read the reasons next to each flag.
steps.detail: 'Needs support' is a rule-based flag (no readiness score, not enough evidence, or a High-priority gap), not a prediction.

steps.do: Use the authoring pages (Assessments, Question bank, Learning resources, Interview questions, Knowledge base) to fix the gaps you see.

result: Know who needs help and why.

problems.fix: No students are assigned to you yet; ask the operator.

procedures.title: HOD: review your departments
procedures.summary: Aggregates only for your assigned departments.
before: An admin has assigned your departments.

steps.do: Click **HOD dashboard** in the menu.
Choose the **Department** and read counts, averages and the skill heatmap. Individual student records are never shown.

result: Department-level picture.

problems.fix: Ask the admin to add your departments under HOD assignments.

procedures.title: What the numbers and labels mean
procedures.summary: A glossary of every score, level and status.

terms.meaning: Your result on assessment questions for a skill, calculated with the assessment's scoring rules (including negative marking if set).
A weighted combination of skill scores using your college's active readiness rule, shown with the rule version.
The band your score falls into, from the college's level thresholds.
Too few relevant assessment results to give a trustworthy score. Take more assessments.
Derived from the college's gap thresholds.

A comparison of your academic records with a job's rules. Per criterion: Met, Not met or Unknown (missing data). Overall: Meets configured criteria, Does not meet configured criteria, Some data missing, or No automatic criteria.
How your skills match a job's required skills. Not the same as eligibility.
The approved document and passage an Assistant answer or search result came from.
A rule-based flag on the faculty dashboard, not a prediction.

procedures.title: What is not in this version
procedures.summary: Known limits so nothing surprises you.

terms.meaning: Not available. The Assistant is rule-based and cites approved documents.
Not available. Knowledge search is keyword-based.
Not available. Scanned PDFs and images are not read.
There is still no screen to add departments after install; that uses the API (/api/v1/admin/departments). There is also no way to deactivate a user from a screen yet.
Only password reset (when email is configured).
